newsitem.title: USA: Boeing off sharply after Q1 results. [CORRECTED 01:10 GMT 29/4]
newsitem.headline: Boeing off sharply after Q1 results. [CORRECTED 01:10 GMT 29/4]

text.p: Boeing Co. shares fell sharply in early U.S. trade on Monday after the company reported first quarter results and the market reacted to a report of possible merger of Boeing competitors Lockheed Martin and Airbus Industrie.

Boeing shares opened at $94.25, down $7.75 (corrects share price and fall), on the New York Stock Exchange, contributing to a fall of 24 points in the Dow Jones industrial average, which was at 6,714 in early trading.
"The stock is down because earnings came in quite a bit below the consensus. That's it in a nutshell," said Peter Jacobs, an analyst at Ragan MacKenzie in Seattle.

Boeing said excluding a one-time gain of $64 million, it earned $313 million, or 87 cents a share in the first quarter. Analysts surveyed by First Call had expected Boeing to post income of $1 a share.

In addition, the London Times reported Saturday that Airbus and Lockheed Martin were discussing a possible merger. And, the European Union and U.S. officials have begun talks on European complaints about U.S. subsidies to aircraft makers, and Boeing fears the outcome will be linked to an EU decision on its planned takeover of McDonnell Douglas Corp., traders said.
"The earnings are not quite up to par, and the other stories are not helping," said a trader, who added that there were concerns on Wall Street about the company's future operating margins.
